reason: H0 fuzzes standalone JSON token decoding and a contiguous zlib stream, but S1 contains a separate stdin-driven PNG/IDAT processing path whose chunk semantics and fragmented zlib protocol are not exercised. In particular, H0 never drives IDAT boundaries by incrementally changing source meta.wi and meta.closed after wuffs_base__suspension__short_read.
evidence: S1 main validates the PNG signature in src_buffer_array and passes the remaining bytes to process_png_chunks.
process_png_chunks parses attacker-controlled chunk_len and chunk_type, handles IHDR and IDAT, copies IDAT payloads into idat_buffer_array, and records boundaries in idat_splits.

decode_once(frag_dst, frag_idat) explicitly tests four fragmentation configurations; its frag_idat path exposes successive idat_splits by updating idat.meta.wi and idat.meta.closed on wuffs_base__suspension__short_read.

H0 zlib_fuzzer.c calls wuffs_zlib__decoder__transform_io with the supplied src as one stream and only loops on wuffs_base__suspension__short_write; it does not implement the short_read boundary protocol used by decode_once.
H0 json_fuzzer.c targets wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and does not cover the PNG/IDAT entry path.
recommended_action: Add a harness for the S1 PNG/IDAT path, or extend the zlib harness to derive multiple source boundaries from fuzz input and exercise short_read transitions by advancing meta.wi and closed; include malformed PNG chunk lengths/types and fragmented IDAT sequences.
